title: High-resolution mapping of DNA alkylation damage and base excision repair at yeast transcription factor binding sites
authors: Mingrui Duan; Smitha Sivapragasam; Jacob S. Antony; Jenna Ulibarri; John M. Hinz; Gregory M.K. Poon; John J. Wyrick; Peng Mao
one_liner_zh: 该文用NMP-seq研究酵母转录因子结合位点的DNA烷基化损伤与碱基切除修复，虽涉及TF-DNA互作但无AI或物理模拟方法，属纯实验测序研究，与本课题方法轴不匹配。
abstract: DNA base damage arises frequently in living cells and needs to be removed by base excision repair (BER) to prevent mutagenesis and genome instability. Both the formation and repair of base damage occur in chromatin and are conceivably affected by DNA-binding proteins such as transcription factors (TFs). However, to what extent TF binding affects base damage distribution and BER in cells is unclear. Here, we used a genome-wide damage mapping method, N -methylpurine-sequencing (NMP-seq), to characterize alkylation damage distribution and BER at TF binding sites in yeast cells treated with the alkylating agent methyl methanesulfonate (MMS). Our data shows that alkylation damage formation was mainly suppressed at the binding sites of yeast TFs Abf1 and Reb1, but individual hotspots with elevated damage levels were also found. Additionally, Abf1 and Reb1 binding strongly inhibits BER in vivo and in vitro , causing slow repair both within the core motif and its adjacent DNA. The observed effects are caused by the TF-DNA interaction, because damage formation and BER can be restored by depletion of Abf1 or Reb1 protein from the nucleus. Thus, our data reveal that TF binding significantly modulates alkylation base damage formation and inhibits repair by the BER pathway. The interplay between base damage formation and BER may play an important role in affecting mutation frequency in gene regulatory regions.
abstract_zh: DNA碱基损伤在活细胞中频繁发生，需要通过碱基切除修复（base excision repair, BER）来清除，以防止突变发生和基因组不稳定。碱基损伤的形成和修复均发生在染色质中，并可能受到DNA结合蛋白（如转录因子（transcription factors, TFs））的影响。然而，TF结合在细胞中对碱基损伤分布和BER的影响程度尚不清楚。在此，我们使用全基因组损伤定位方法——N-甲基嘌呤测序（N-methylpurine-sequencing, NMP-seq），来表征经烷化剂甲基磺酸甲酯（methyl methanesulfonate, MMS）处理的酵母细胞中TF结合位点的烷化损伤分布和BER。我们的数据显示，烷化损伤的形成主要在酵母TF Abf1和Reb1的结合位点处受到抑制，但也发现了损伤水平升高的个别热点。此外，Abf1和Reb1的结合在体内和体外均强烈抑制BER，导致核心基序及其邻近DNA区域的修复缓慢。观察到的效应是由TF-DNA相互作用引起的，因为从细胞核中耗竭Abf1或Reb1蛋白可以恢复损伤形成和BER。因此，我们的数据揭示，TF结合显著调节烷化碱基损伤的形成，并抑制BER途径的修复。碱基损伤形成与BER之间的相互作用可能在影响基因调控区域的突变频率中发挥重要作用。
